title: Short Stuff: Charity Tips
summary: Short Stuff episode offering year-end charity giving advice. Hosts explain how to vet charities using watchdog sites (CharityWatch, GiveWell, Charity Navigator), checking annual report outcome sections, focusing on evidence, cost-effectiveness, transparency, and being underfunded, and judging efficiency by percentages (about 60% or more to program services) rather than raw dollar figures. They discuss GiveWell's focus on global health and poverty (e.g., insecticide-treated malaria nets), the example of Co-ED (Cooperative for Education) as an efficient, underfunded charity, whether to spread donations or give one larger gift, giving consistent amounts annually, avoiding scams and look-alike names (Breast Cancer Research Foundation vs. Breast Cancer Research and Support Foundation), recognizing that nonprofits are businesses that can be poorly run, and balancing local giving with global charities.

segments.title: Year-end charity scramble and vetting sites
segments.summary: Josh introduces the episode as helpful tips for choosing charities at year end. He recommends watchdog sites like CharityWatch, GiveWell, and Charity Navigator, and checking a charity's annual report outcomes section for concrete results.

segments.title: Criteria for effective charities
segments.summary: GiveWell's criteria are described: evidence-based impact, cost-effectiveness, transparency, and being underfunded. The hosts note GiveWell focuses on global health and poverty, and that small donations can buy things like insecticide-treated nets against malaria.

segments.title: Judging overhead and efficiency by percentages
segments.summary: The hosts explain that executive pay, overhead, and fundraising costs should be judged as percentages of budget, with a recommended minimum of about 60% going to direct program services. They warn that very low spending on overhead can mean a charity is running on a shoestring. Co-ED is cited as an example, with about 85% going to programs, nine cents spent per dollar raised, and funds lasting about 1.57 years.

segments.title: Spreading donations and consistent giving
segments.summary: The hosts discuss whether to give small amounts to several charities or one larger gift, concluding it is a personal choice as long as each charity is researched. They suggest giving roughly the same amount at the same time each year so charities can budget.

segments.title: Avoiding scams, look-alike names, and poorly run charities
segments.summary: The hosts note that the FTC found over a hundred actions against dozens of fraudulent charities, many claiming to serve veterans. They warn about similarly named charities, contrasting Breast Cancer Research Foundation (A+ from CharityWatch, about seven dollars spent per dollar raised) with Breast Cancer Research and Support Foundation (F, about 8% programming, $87 spent per $100 collected). They also note well-meaning charities can be poorly managed.

segments.title: Local versus global giving
segments.summary: The hosts advise not to overlook global charities in favor of local ones, suggesting considering both. They suggest pairing a local cause, like neighborhood tree planting, with a large global cause in the same area.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts encourage listeners to give to good charities and close the episode.
